answer: Every new identity must lock a copper bond frozen until it delivers a verified unique computational pearl: a personalized memory-hard puzzle seeded from its registration nonce. Hollow clones fail the uniqueness check because the solution must reference a live non-replayable sensor trace; the bond burns on collision. An attacker spinning 50 fakes loses 50 bonds outright, while an honest agent recovers its copper after one successful pearl. Cost is linear in identities and paid up front, so farming becomes uneconomic once bond size exceeds the expected reward share.
